pr_title: [WIP] Resolve imports from paths also specified in LESS config
pr_body:
Use similar file resolution strategy as [LESS FileManager](https://github.com/less/less.js/blob/v2.7.3/lib/less-node/file-manager.js#L23)

Fixes #1818
pr_comments: Might have to modify a little, it's based on the resolution strategy from [2.7.3](https://github.com/less/less.js/blob/v2.7.3/lib/less-node/file-manager.js#L23), but the version in 3.0.1 (which Parcel uses) uses a [slightly modified version](https://github.com/less/less.js/blob/master/lib/less-node/file-manager.js#L19).

issue_context.title: [LESSAsset] Respect included paths in LESS config
issue_context.body:
# 🐛 bug report

When specifying a config for LESS compiler/renderer, the `paths` property in the config is not respected/resolved the way LESS does itself. You can specify the property to lessc with `--include-path=path1:path2:path3` or via the config (.lessrc / .lessrc.js / package.json key "less"): `{ "paths": ["path1", "path2", "path3"] }`

## 🤔 Expected Behavior

When you have included a path in the config that is outside of entry file or `rootDir`, you would want to search/visit those directories - like LESS does.

When running: `lessc --include-path=src/:node_modules/semantic-ui-less/ src/index.less` I get the following:

```
FileError: 'theme.less' wasn't found. Tried - src/theme.less,node_modules/semantic-ui-less/the
me.less,theme.less in src/index.less on line 1, column 1:
1 @import 'theme.less';
```

## 😯 Current Behavior

LESSAsset doesn't respect the `paths` property in the config, so when I run Parcel I get:

```
×  src/index.less: Cannot find module './theme.less' from 'src'
```

## 💁 Possible Solution

The solution to this problem, would be to change the `loadFile` function in `LESSAsset.js` and add the `options` parameter (which is the LESS option/config, containing the LESS config object retrieved earlier).

```
async loadFile(filename, currentDirectory) {
    filename = parseCSSImport(filename);
    let resolved = await resolver.resolve(
    filename,
    path.join(currentDirectory, 'index')
    );
    return {
    contents: await fs.readFile(resolved.path, 'utf8'),
    filename: resolved.path
    };
}
```

## 🔦 Context

Semantic UI has this weird way of merge'ing default themes and variable files with customized, by importing files relatively and depending on paths from the upper context. That's why you have to tell LESS to search for those files in another directories, because they don't exist from relative location where they are imported. See image below.

![](https://i.imgur.com/0tsPikK.png)

## 🌍 Your Environment

<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->

| Software         | Version(s) |
| ---------------- | ---------- |
| Parcel           | 1.9.7
| Node             | 10.7.0
| npm/Yarn         | 1.7.0
| Operating System | Win10
